//: MOBILE. The desktop config is the sibling file; this one exists because
CLAUDE.md says a working mobile experience is not optional, and nothing was
measuring it. There is no preset here on purpose — mobile is what Lighthouse
does by default: 412x823, simulated slow 4G, and a 4x CPU slowdown on top of
everything that already costs this site its desktop score.
MOBILE PERFORMANCE IS A WARNING, NOT A GATE, AND HERE IS THE EVIDENCE.
Medians of the same page, on this runner, with nothing between the readings
that touches the render path:
3 runs    desktop 54    mobile 68
7 runs    desktop 58    mobile 71
7 runs    desktop 58    mobile 66
Desktop with seven samples repeats exactly, so it keeps a hard floor at
0.55. Mobile does not: two seven-run medians five points apart. Going to
fifteen runs would cost twenty minutes a push and narrow that interval, not
close it.
A gate on a number with that spread fails at random, and a check that fails
at random gets ignored — which is worse than having no check, because it
still looks like coverage. So this warns, and the number is printed into the
run summary by tools/resumo-lighthouse.mjs on every push. Nothing is hidden;
it just no longer stops a build it cannot reliably judge.
This is the honest version of a floor that would otherwise be lowered every
few pushes. The day seven runs land within two points of each other, it goes
back to being an error.
WHAT DOES STOP A BUILD HERE is what measured stably across every run:
accessibility 96, SEO 100, layout shift 0.002–0.006. Those are errors and
they are nowhere near their limits, which is the point — they fail only if
something real breaks.
The paint ceilings are deliberately loose. FCP was asserted at 1.5s from a
run that measured 1.02s, and the next run measured 2.4s and failed on it —
the same mistake as the performance floor, one metric down. They now sit far
enough out to catch a regression and not a bad afternoon on a shared runner.
History worth keeping: a 0.38 floor once caught a real regression at 35–36
and it was fixed rather than lowered. Before the mobile work this page
scored 40 with a 7.1s LCP. See PERFORMANCE.md for all of it.
